name: feedback-14-ci-workflow
body:
source: section-helpers/feedback-14 on solution.component.ci-workflow (spec reconciliation, traceability).

SOURCE STATEMENT (feedback-14): the `realised-by` edge from domain.service.publish-release to solution.component.ci-workflow does not fit the component. publish-release is defined only as a tag-triggered release ("on a consented tag … build one binary per supported target … publish … update the package manifests"), and its driving requirement requirements.requirement.native-ci-verification is also release-scoped ("Every release runs…"; AC: "before the Release is published, the release workflow shows one green native e2e job per supported target"). ci-workflow is the PR/push gate in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (gofmt, go vet, make build, module-path guard, go test, then the native-e2e call): it publishes nothing and does not run on a tag, so no part of publish-release's body describes it. The module-path guard actually enforces requirements.requirement.source-repo's AC, which drives domain.group.distribution, not publish-release. Then correction of solution.note.workflow-file-ownership, whose claim that ci-workflow "mirrors native-e2e-ci and release-workflow" is inaccurate.

RESOLUTION [with user] — option (1) of the feedback, the cleaner option: add a domain node for continuous verification of pushes/PRs and realise ci-workflow from it, rather than widening publish-release's release-scoped body.
- Added domain.service.verify-changes, contained by domain.group.distribution (where publish-release sits), describing the ci.yml push/PR gate: gofmt, go vet, make build, the module-path guard, go test ./... (unit/integration/e2e) and the native-e2e job that delegates to the reusable native-e2e.yml. It publishes nothing and does not run on a tag — explicitly distinct from publish-release.
- Drove it by the requirements it serves: requirements.requirement.source-repo (its AC — go.mod declares exactly github.com/really-knows-ai/kalide and all internal imports use it — is enforced by the module-path guard); requirements.requirement.native-ci-verification (the native e2e verification, run here on every push/PR via the reusable workflow; ci-workflow's own body cites it); and requirements.requirement.distribution (the pipeline requirement — kalide is "built, verified" through a defined distribution pipeline with native-CI verification — which grounds the build/test gates, since no dedicated host-CI-gate requirement exists in the requirement tree).
- Added `realised-by domain.service.verify-changes -> solution.component.ci-workflow`; removed `realised-by domain.service.publish-release -> solution.component.ci-workflow`. publish-release keeps its release/tag realisations through solution.component.release-workflow and solution.component.native-e2e-ci, matching its body.
- Updated solution.component.ci-workflow's body: the closing "Realises domain.service.publish-release alongside its sibling native-e2e-ci and release-workflow" became "Realises domain.service.verify-changes … not domain.service.publish-release, which is tag/release-scoped; the module-path guard enforces requirements.requirement.source-repo's AC and the native-e2e job delegates to solution.component.native-e2e-ci."
- Corrected solution.note.workflow-file-ownership: its RESOLUTION bullet claimed ci-workflow was "realised-by domain.service.publish-release — mirroring native-e2e-ci and release-workflow, whose driving requirement is requirements.requirement.native-ci-verification". The bullet now records the corrected realisation and an UPDATE paragraph (section-helpers/feedback-14) marks the earlier claim superseded, stating that native-e2e-ci and release-workflow run as part of a release while ci-workflow does not.

Invariant check: every solution.component still has >=1 implemented-by (ci-workflow -> `.github/workflows/ci.yml`); domain.service.verify-changes has >=1 drives edge and >=1 realised-by edge; domain.group.distribution still contains publish-release and now verify-changes; no requirement or other node's prose changed.
